name: Shamsi Gorge
near: The villages of Koshoy and Shamshy where the gorge opens into the Chu Valley; the city of Tokmok is further down the valley. From Bishkek it is about 100–105 km (too.kg, hiking.kg). The earlier value “Karagul ~6.2 km” was calculated from an erroneous catalogue point.
elev: Shamsi Pass — 3570 m (eurasia.travel); the lower part of the gorge where it opens into the Chu Valley — about 1000–1500 m (estimate, not confirmed). The elevation gain on walking routes from the parking lot is up to 300 m (hiking.kg).
short: Shamsi is a little-known wooded gorge of the Shamshy River on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Range ~100 km east of Bishkek, with the side gorge of Tuyuk, spruce forests and a pass into the Kochkor valley.
desc: Shamsi Gorge (Shamshy) stretches from the Chu Valley near the villages of Koshoy and Shamshy south to Shamsi Pass (3570 m), which historically linked the Chu and Kochkor valleys. The slopes are covered with dense coniferous forests, with subalpine meadows higher up; the side river Tuyuk, with a cascade of waterfalls and a lake at its head, flows into the gorge (24.kg, 2017). Wild boar, lynx, hares and ermine live here (eurasia.travel). The gorge is associated with the Shamshy hoard: in 1958 a gold mask from a woman's burial was found in a burial mound at its mouth — according to local legend, the mask of “Princess Shamsi” (24.kg). Too.kg mentions the “Shah's house”, built in 1968 for a visit by the Shah of Iran. There is no infrastructure: no shops, cafes or guesthouses — only places for tents and picnics.
guide: Shamsi is for those who want forest and quiet two hours from Bishkek without the crowds of Ala-Archa. Leave your car at the parking lot in the gorge and walk along the Shamsi or turn into the Tuyuk valley: 2–8 km, up to 300 m of gain, easy trails. Ask locals about the 1968 “Shah's house” — it was built for a visit by the Shah of Iran. Remember that a gold mask was found in a burial mound at the mouth of the gorge in 1958 — according to legend, that of “Princess Shamsi”. There's no signal and no shops, so bring everything with you and don't forget to take your litter out.
see: Coniferous forests and the Shamsi river valley; the side gorge of Tuyuk with a cascade of waterfalls (24.kg); viewpoints and picnic spots (hiking.kg); the 1968 “Shah's house” (too.kg); for the experienced — Shamsi Pass (3570 m) and treks toward Song-Kol (silkroadexplore).
skip: You need infrastructure — cafes, guesthouses and mobile signal are absent here. You have no car: there is no public transport into the gorge. You're looking for “wow” views of glaciers — Shamsi is more of a calm forest gorge.
diff: A walk in the lower valley is relatively easy; crossings of high passes are separate, demanding routes.
when: May — October: the dirt road is passable, the meadows are green (May — June) or golden (September — October). In winter and in the muddy season the road in the upper reaches and the fords become hard to pass (editorial, based on hiking.kg on fords).
hours: A natural area with no regime and no barrier with a fee (too.kg: free entry). The sources mention no access restrictions.
daytime: Morning — fewer cars on the dirt road and soft light in the forest; for a night in a tent — the evening by the river (editorial).
how: Via Tokmok, Koshoy and Shamshy; then along the river. Choose where to park according to the condition of the dirt road and your car's capabilities.
needcar: To get there — a private car or a booked car; Too.kg doesn't mention any regular transport into the gorge.
self: Yes: free entry, no permits needed (too.kg). You need your own or a booked car, preferably with good ground clearance.
roadtype: A dirt road along the Shamsi and Tuyuk, deteriorating in the upper reaches; there are fords.
traveltime: Hiking.kg guideline: 105 km / 2 hours from Bishkek; walks from the parking lot — up to 7.8 km and 2 h 20 min for the chosen option, gain up to 300 m.
stay: The source describes tent camps; it doesn't confirm any operating hotels or bookings in the gorge itself.
net: Too.kg's description says there is no signal; the date of the check and the operator are not given.
entry: Too.kg calls entry free but gives no effective date. There is no confirmed rate for 2026.
transfer: Not confirmed: no 2025–2026 prices for a taxi/transfer to Shamsi were found. Guidelines: a taxi Bishkek — Burana 1500–2200 som one way (asiaodysseytravel 2026, a nearby destination); Sputnik8 tours “Tuyuk Gorge and the Burana Tower” — $210 per group.
bring: All your food and water (no shops; boil river water — too.kg), a tent and warm clothes for a night out, an offline map (no signal), shoes you don't mind getting wet at the fords, litter bags.
warn: There is no mobile signal (too.kg) — tell someone your route. Fords and a deteriorating dirt road in the upper reaches; after rain the road turns soggy (hiking.kg). Drink river water only after boiling — livestock graze here. Shamsi Pass (3570 m) is a serious mountain route, not a stroll.
food: There are no cafes in the gorge (too.kg). Bring food with you; the nearest eateries are in Tokmok and roadside cafes on the Bishkek — Balykchy highway (editorial). In summer you can ask shepherds for kumis.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 20 ratings/reviews per the card's counter as of 03.10.2026. The review texts were not used to confirm prices, roads or safety.
p.sum: Shamsi is a forest gorge with no infrastructure ≈100–110 km (≈2 h) from Bishkek via Tokmok and the villages of Koshoy/Shamshy: there is no public transport into the gorge, so you need your own car with good clearance (further up the gorge it is dirt road and fords) or a jeep tour (Sputnik8/Tripster $210–235, €206 per car). The most interesting format is a horse ride to Shamsi Pass with lunch with a family (Eurasia Travel, $130–315/person). There is no signal, shops or cafes — bring food, water and a gas stove; the best time is May — October.

p.iti.3.title: Combinations

p.season: May — June: greenery, high water at the fords. July — August: warm, a dry road. September — October: golden autumn, the best weather for walks. November — April: the upper reaches and fords are hard to pass, snow.
p.budget.economy: ≈1500–3000 som/person: your own/rented car shared (fuel ≈200 km), food from home; marshrutka (minibus) to Tokmok 100 + a taxi in the gorge (price not found).
p.budget.comfort: A jeep tour $210–235 per car (up to 4 people) or the Eurasia horse tour $130–315/person.
p.permits: No permit is needed; entry is free per too.kg (the Eurasia tour mentions an “entrance fee” — check on site, keep cash).
p.access: With children — yes for a picnic and short walks (the horse tour — from age 10); older people — near the parking lot; stroller — no; with a dog — yes, on a leash near livestock.
